title: Synthesis of a new lithium ionic conductor, thio-LISICON – lithium germanium sul

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper discusses a Ga-substituted thio-LISICON solid solution written as Li(Ge0.75Ga0.25)S4 only in the form of the general formula Li_{4-1x} (Ge_{1-δ}Ga_δ)S4 (with x=0.25 mentioned as giving highest conductivity) and examples like Li4.34Ge0.75Ga0.25S4. It does not explicitly state the specific target formula exactly as “Li(Ge0.75Ga0.25)S4” (i.e., with Li=1). The extracted formula has the wrong lithium stoichiometry relative to what is reported (Li ≈ 4−x, not 1).
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Li4.34Ge0.75Ga0.25S4 (example composition shown in Fig. 4) or, for x=0.25 in the general solid solution, Li3.75(Ge0.75Ga0.25)S4 (from Li_{4-x}(Ge0.75Ga0.25)S4 with x=0.25).

entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Li2GeS3 or Li2ZnGeS4 (depending on intended target); Table 1 does not contain Li4GeS4.

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: Table 1 (the alleged provenance) lists a compound in the Li2S–Ga2S3 system as “Li5GaS4” (with reported conductivity 5.1×10^-28 S cm^-1 at 100°C). However, the extracted value is “Li5GaS4” (Ga), while the table and the paper consistently use gallium as “Ga” and sulfur as “S”; the formula shown is “Li5GaS4” only if read correctly. The extracted value has “Li5GaS4” with 'Ga' present, but the table actually shows “Li5GaS4” exactly—wait: the table entry is “Li5GaS4” (Li5 GaS4). On closer inspection, the table row reads “Li5GaS4” (i.e., Li5GaS4), not “Li5GaS4” with any different element. Therefore the extracted value matches. (If the extractor meant Li5GaS4 but wrote Li5GaS4, it's the same.)

In the Experimental section, the paper explicitly lists Li2S among the starting materials (“The starting materials were Li2S, GeS2, ZnS and Ga2S3 ...”). However, it does not provide a specific mass, moles, or quantity for Li2S—only that the starting materials were “weighed... in appropriate molar ratios.” Therefore, the extractor’s claim that the amount is not specified is supported.

The paper explicitly identifies GeS2 as a starting material in the Experimental section: “The starting materials were Li2S, GeS2, ZnS and Ga2S3…”. However, no mass, moles, or other specific quantity of GeS2 is given—only that starting materials were “weighed, mixed in appropriate molar ratios.” Therefore the chemical identity (GeS2) is supported and the extracted note that the amount is not specified is also supported.

In the Experimental section, ZnS is explicitly listed as one of the starting materials: “The starting materials were Li2S, GeS2, ZnS and Ga2S3… These were weighed, mixed in appropriate molar ratios…”. However, the paper does not provide a specific mass (g, mg) or molar amount for ZnS; it only states that reagents were mixed in “appropriate molar ratios” without detailing the ZnS quantity. Therefore, identifying ZnS with amount not specified is consistent with the source text.

In the Experimental section, the paper explicitly lists Ga2S3 (written as “Ga S3” with subscript 2) among the starting materials: “The starting materials were Li2S, GeS2, ZnS and Ga2S3…”. However, the text provides no masses, molar amounts, or quantities for Ga2S3—only that materials were “weighed, mixed in appropriate molar ratios.” Therefore, the identity is supported and the amount being “Not specified in text” is also supported.

Table 1 (in the Results and discussion section on page 2) explicitly lists the crystal system as “Orthorhombic” for multiple compounds in the thio-LISICON lithium germanium sulfide system (e.g., Li4GeS4, Li2GeS3, Li2ZnGeS4, etc.). Therefore the extracted XRD crystal_system = orthorhombic is supported (though it applies to several compounds, including the noted Li4GeS4).

The paper explicitly reports the lattice parameters for orthorhombic Li3GeS4 in the X-ray Rietveld refinement results (Table 2 footnote): a = 14.0658(2) Å, b = 7.75102(15) Å, c = 6.14973(10) Å. These match the extracted values (rounded). Although the provenance says 'Table 2', the values are indeed given with Table 2 (in the space group/lattice parameter line).

The paper reports room-temperature ionic conductivity for Li(Ge0.75Ga0.25)S4 as 6.5×10^-3 S cm^-1 (i.e., 6.5 mS cm^-1). This appears in the Abstract (“6.5 × 10^-3 S cm^-1 at room temperature”), Table 1 (“6.5 × 10^-3 … at x=0.25”), and Results text near Fig. 5(b) (“conductivity value at 25°C was 6.53 × 10^-3 S cm^-1”). The extracted numeric value 6.5 mS cm^-1 is correct, but the note claiming the exponent is ambiguous is not supported by the text; the exponent is explicitly −3 in multiple places.

This appears in the discussion of Fig. 6 and the Fig. 6 caption: "No significant anodic current due to electrolyte decomposition was observed up to 5 V" and "stable for an applied voltage up to 5 V" (vs. Li).

The paper reports a Hebb–Wagner polarization measurement and gives an electronic conductivity value at an applied voltage of 1.0 V. However, the extracted value is None, and the source text does contain a readable numeric value: “the electronic conductivity at an applied voltage of 1.0 V was 6.8×10^-28 S cm^-1” (page 6, discussing Fig. 7). Therefore, the extraction as None is only supported insofar as Fig. 7 itself (the plotted figure) is not provided here and could be unreadable, but the value is explicitly stated in the body text.
